messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Stanbox!
parts:
So I talked with Alan Edelman and he’s psyched about Stanbox. He suggested we make a mockup—a Stanbox-looking object with a particular model that would help sell the concept. What would be a good example? 8 schools seems too simple. The pharmacology example is ok (if Novartis gives permission to use it) but maybe it’s too complicated? I’d like to have a real example—a real problem with real data, where the model makes sense and can be clearly described. Any thoughts?
A

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: Stanbox!
parts:
On Friday, March 6, 2015 at 11:58:16 PM UTC+1, Andrew Gelman wrote:
> So I talked with Alan Edelman and he’s psyched about Stanbox. He suggested we make a mockup—a Stanbox-looking object with a particular model that would help sell the concept. What would be a good example? 8 schools seems too simple. The pharmacology example is ok (if Novartis gives permission to use it) but maybe it’s too complicated? I’d like to have a real example—a real problem with real data, where the model makes sense and can be clearly described. Any thoughts?
> A

Theophylline pharmacokinetics? The data is published, is real and really fitted a thousand times. Also: You can showcase it using a so-called transit model for which I got in the special case of a single oral dose an analytic solution. This solution is horribly complex and almost for sure not doable in other contenders around due to the special functions needed. Then you could add an ODE base solution to the problem which is a lot easier to write down mathematically, but make the computer sweat.

Sebastian

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Stanbox!
parts:
I think a simple non-hierarchical logistic regression would be
OK or even a simpler linear regression.

As a computer scientist, I really like my "hello world" examples.
Everything else winds up bringing in all kinds of details (like
bernoulli_logit or the inv_logit function for logistic regression).

- Bob
